chapter_title: Software Engineering and Object-Oriented Analysis & Design

topics.title: Software Characteristics & Quality Attributes
topics.content:
Software Characteristics:
- Software is developed, not manufactured in a factory[cite: 1].
- Software does not wear out physically like hardware; it deteriorates over time due to modifications and updates introducing new bugs[cite: 1].
- Software is complex, intangible, malleable, and largely custom-built[cite: 1].

Software Quality Attributes ("CRISP MURTI"):
- Correctness (fulfills specifications), Reliability (consistent operation without failure), Efficiency (optimal resource usage), Integrity (security against unauthorized access), Usability (ease of learning/use)[cite: 1].
- Maintainability (ease of modification), Portability (runs across different platforms), Reusability (components used elsewhere), Interoperability (integrates with other systems), Testability (ease of executing tests)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Software Process Models & CASE Tools
topics.content:
Process Models:
- Waterfall Model: Linear, sequential; heavy documentation; rigid and poor for changing requirements[cite: 1].
- V-Model (Verification & Validation): Early testing planning; verification (left side: "building product RIGHT?") paired in parallel with validation (right side: "building RIGHT product?")[cite: 1].
- Iterative Model: Repeated development cycles yielding working releases per iteration[cite: 1].
- Prototype Model: Quick throwaway or evolutionary mockups built to clarify ambiguous requirements[cite: 1].
- Agile Model: Customer collaboration, incremental delivery (Sprints 2-4 weeks), adaptive to change[cite: 1]. Roles in Scrum include Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Development Team (no traditional Project Manager)[cite: 1].
- Big Bang Model: Lacks formal planning or process; highly risky and unpredictable[cite: 1].

CASE Tools:
- Upper CASE: Supports requirements & design[cite: 1].
- Lower CASE: Supports coding & testing[cite: 1].
- Integrated CASE (I-CASE): Supports entire software lifecycle[cite: 1].

topics.title: Requirements Engineering & SRS Document
topics.content:
Types of Requirements:
- Functional: Specific system behaviors and features (WHAT the system does)[cite: 1].
- Non-Functional ("PURPS"): Constraints and quality attributes (HOW system performs: Performance, Usability, Reliability, Portability, Security)[cite: 1].
- User vs. System: User requirements use plain natural language for customers; System requirements provide technical specs for developers[cite: 1].

Software Requirements Specification (SRS):
- IEEE standard specification document serving as a contract[cite: 1].
- Characteristics ("CUCVM²T"): Correct, Unambiguous, Complete, Consistent, Verifiable, Modifiable, Traceable[cite: 1].

Elicitation, Validation & Management:
- Elicitation Techniques: Interviews, Questionnaires, Observation, Prototyping, Brainstorming, JAD, Use Cases[cite: 1].
- Validation: Requirements reviews, prototyping, test case generation[cite: 1].
- Management: Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) tracks requirements from origin to code/testing[cite: 1].

topics.title: Design Principles, Coupling & Cohesion
topics.content:
Core Design Principles:
- Abstraction (Procedural & Data), Modularity, Information Hiding (Parnas principle), Stepwise Refinement (top-down)[cite: 1].
- Golden Rule: Good design requires LOW Coupling + HIGH Cohesion[cite: 1].

Coupling (Interdependence between modules - Worst to Best):
- Content (one module modifies another's internals) $\rightarrow$ Common (global data) $\rightarrow$ Control (flag passing) $\rightarrow$ Stamp (data structures) $\rightarrow$ Data (simple parameters)[cite: 1].

Cohesion (Internal module focus - Best to Worst):
- Functional (single task) $\rightarrow$ Sequential $\rightarrow$ Communicational $\rightarrow$ Procedural $\rightarrow$ Temporal $\rightarrow$ Logical $\rightarrow$ Coincidental (unrelated tasks)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Architectural Styles & Reference Models
topics.content:
System Organization Styles:
- Repository Model: Subsystems access central shared data store (IDE, DBMS)[cite: 1].
- Client-Server Model: Servers provide services to clients; Thin clients handle presentation while Fat clients process logic[cite: 1].
- Layered Architecture: Each layer provides services to the layer directly above it[cite: 1].

Control & Decomposition Styles:
- Centralized Control: Call-Return model, Manager model[cite: 1].
- Event-Based Control: Broadcast model, Interrupt-driven model[cite: 1].
- Reference Architectures: MVC (Model-data, View-UI, Controller-logic), Pipe and Filter, Microkernel, Blackboard[cite: 1].
- Real-Time Systems: Hard Real-Time (deadline miss = system failure) vs. Soft Real-Time (deadline miss = degraded performance)[cite: 1].

subsections.title: SOFTWARE TESTING, COST ESTIMATION, QUALITY & CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT

topics.title: Testing Fundamentals & Test Case Design
topics.content:
Testing Levels:
- Unit Testing: Individual modules tested in isolation by developers using Drivers (call module) and Stubs (simulate called modules)[cite: 1].
- Integration Testing: Combined modules tested via Big Bang, Top-Down (requires stubs), Bottom-Up (requires drivers), or Sandwich approaches[cite: 1].
- System Testing: Complete integrated system evaluation (Functional, Performance, Security)[cite: 1].
- Acceptance Testing: Alpha (internal users at developer site) and Beta (actual users at customer site)[cite: 1].

Test Case Design Techniques:
- Black-Box (Functional): Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis (BVA - tests min, max, boundaries), Decision Tables, Use Case Testing[cite: 1].
- White-Box (Structural): Code-level coverage; Path Coverage > Branch Coverage > Statement Coverage[cite: 1].

topics.title: Software Metrics, Cost Estimation & Quality Standards
topics.content:
Cost Estimation & Metrics:
- COCOMO I: Basic Effort $E = a \times (KLOC)^b$ (Organic: $2.4 \times KLOC^{1.05}$, Semi-detached, Embedded)[cite: 1].
- Cyclomatic Complexity (McCabe): $V(G) = E - N + 2P$ ($E$=edges, $N$=nodes, $P$=components)[cite: 1].
- Defect Density = Defects / KLOC[cite: 1].

Quality Assurance & CMMI:
- SQA Techniques: Formal Technical Reviews (Inspection - highest formality; Walkthrough; Desk Check - lowest)[cite: 1].
- Pareto Principle: 80% of defects stem from 20% of root causes[cite: 1].
- CMMI Maturity Levels ("I Must Do Quality Optimization"): Level 1 Initial $\rightarrow$ Level 2 Managed $\rightarrow$ Level 3 Defined $\rightarrow$ Level 4 Quantitatively Managed $\rightarrow$ Level 5 Optimizing[cite: 1].
- ISO Standards: ISO 9001 (generic process), ISO/IEC 9126 / ISO 25010 (software quality characteristics)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Software Configuration Management (SCM)
topics.content:
Configuration Management Concepts:
- Configuration Item (CI): Artifact controlled under SCM (code, SRS, design)[cite: 1].
- Baseline: Approved version of a CI at a specific milestone[cite: 1].
- Change Control Board (CCB): Authority for reviewing and approving change requests[cite: 1].
- Semantic Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (MAJOR: breaking changes, MINOR: new features, PATCH: bug fixes)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Four Pillars of OOP & Modeling Concepts
topics.content:
Four Pillars of OOP ("APIE"):
- Encapsulation: Bundling data and methods while restricting access[cite: 1].
- Abstraction: Hiding complexity by showing essential features[cite: 1].
- Inheritance: Reusing parent class properties in child classes[cite: 1].
- Polymorphism: Compile-time (Method Overloading) vs. Run-time (Method Overriding)[cite: 1].

Relationships:
- Association (general link), Aggregation (hollow diamond ◇: weak "has-a", parts exist independently), Composition (filled diamond ◆: strong "has-a", child destroyed with parent)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Use Case Modeling & Unified Modeling Language (UML)
topics.content:
Use Case Modeling:
- Components: Actor, Use Case, System Boundary[cite: 1].
- Relationships: `<<include>>` (mandatory execution) vs. `<<extend>>` (optional execution)[cite: 1].

UML Diagrams (Three Amigos: Booch, Rumbaugh, Jacobson):
- Structural (Static): Class, Object, Component, Deployment, Package[cite: 1].
- Behavioral (Dynamic): Use Case, Sequence (time-ordered interactions), Collaboration/Communication (relationship-focused), State (object state changes), Activity (flowchart workflow)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Design Patterns & Class Notation
topics.content:
Design Patterns (Gang of Four):
- Creational: Object creation mechanisms (Singleton - single instance; Factory - subclass creation)[cite: 1].
- Structural: Composition of classes/objects (Adapter, Decorator, Facade)[cite: 1].
- Behavioral: Object interactions (Observer - notify state changes; Strategy)[cite: 1].

Design Class Diagrams & Visibility:
- Visibility Indicators: `+` (Public), `-` (Private), `#` (Protected), `~` (Package)[cite: 1].
- Multiplicity: `1` (exactly one), `0..1` (zero or one), `*` (zero or more), `1..*` (one or more)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Mapping Design to Code & Exception Handling
topics.content:
Mapping Design Constructs:
- Class $\rightarrow$ Class definition; Attribute $\rightarrow$ Instance variable; Method $\rightarrow$ Function; Association $\rightarrow$ Reference/pointer (1-to-N uses Collections/Lists)[cite: 1].
- Inheritance: `extends` keyword; Interface implementation: `implements` keyword[cite: 1].

Exception Handling:
- Checked Exceptions: Must be explicitly handled using `try-catch` or declared via `throws`[cite: 1].
- Unchecked Exceptions: Runtime exceptions[cite: 1].
- `finally` block: Code that executes unconditionally for resource cleanup[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of software?
options: Software wears out over time due to physical friction
questions.explanation: Software does not wear out due to physical friction like hardware; it deteriorates over time due to modifications and updates introducing new bugs[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which software process model pairs each development phase directly with a corresponding testing phase?
questions.explanation: The V-Model is also known as the Verification and Validation Model, pairing development phases with parallel testing phases[cite: 1].

questions.question: Evaluating software during development to answer 'Are we building the product RIGHT?' refers to:
questions.explanation: Verification ensures the product is built according to specifications ('building the product right')[cite: 1]. Validation checks if it is the 'right product'[cite: 1].

questions.question: In Scrum methodology, what is the standard typical duration of a Sprint?
questions.explanation: Scrum Sprints are timeboxed iterations typically lasting 2 to 4 weeks[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which requirement specification represents a non-functional requirement?
options: The system shall allow users to log in using email and password
The system shall respond to user requests within 2 seconds
The system shall generate monthly invoice reports
The system shall send order confirmation emails
questions.explanation: Response time (< 2 seconds) specifies system performance, which is a non-functional requirement[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which CASE tool category specifically supports early software lifecycle phases like requirements analysis and design?
questions.explanation: Upper CASE tools support early development phases such as requirements engineering and architectural design[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which design principle proposed by David Parnas states that internal details of a module should be inaccessible to other modules?
questions.explanation: Information Hiding hides internal implementation details behind exposed module interfaces[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which type of module coupling is considered the BEST (most desirable)?
questions.explanation: Data coupling is the best/weakest coupling because modules only pass simple data parameters[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which type of module cohesion is considered the BEST?
questions.explanation: Functional cohesion is the highest/best cohesion, where all elements within a module perform a single well-defined task[cite: 1].

questions.question: In software design, ideal system architecture aims for:
questions.explanation: Good modular design requires Low Coupling (independent modules) and High Cohesion (focused modules)[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which architectural style features a central shared database accessed by multiple subsystems?
questions.explanation: The Repository model centers around a central shared database accessed by independent components[cite: 1].

questions.question: Testing individual modules in isolation by developers is known as:
questions.explanation: Unit testing verifies individual software components or functions in isolation[cite: 1].

questions.question: What testing dummy component simulates a module that is CALLED BY the module under test?
questions.explanation: A Stub simulates lower-level modules called by the module under test[cite: 1]. A Driver calls the module being tested[cite: 1].

questions.question: User Acceptance Testing performed by internal users at the developer's site is called:
questions.explanation: Alpha testing is performed at the developer's site by internal users[cite: 1]. Beta testing occurs at the customer's site with end users[cite: 1].

questions.question: If valid input integers range from 1 to 100, which test input set represents Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)?
questions.explanation: BVA tests boundary boundaries: just below min (0), min (1), max (100), and just above max (101)[cite: 1].

questions.question: McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity V(G) for a control flow graph with E edges, N nodes, and P connected components is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity formula is V(G) = E - N + 2P[cite: 1].

questions.question: In the COCOMO model, which project mode represents small teams working in familiar environments?
questions.explanation: Organic mode applies to small, experienced teams with well-understood requirements[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which level in the CMMI Maturity framework represents 'Defined' processes?
questions.explanation: CMMI Level 3 corresponds to 'Defined' processes established across the organization[cite: 1].

questions.question: The Pareto Principle applied to SQA suggests that:
options: 50% of defects stem from 50% of causes
80% of defects stem from 20% of root causes
100% of defects can be eliminated via reviews
questions.explanation: The Pareto Principle states that roughly 80% of software defects originate from 20% of the code/causes[cite: 1].

questions.question: In semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), when is the MAJOR version number incremented?
options: When backward-compatible bug fixes are made
When new backward-compatible features are added
When incompatible breaking API changes are introduced
questions.explanation: MAJOR version increments when breaking/incompatible API changes are introduced[cite: 1].

questions.question: Method overloading in Object-Oriented Programming is an example of:
questions.explanation: Method overloading (same function name with different parameter signatures) is resolved at compile time (Static Polymorphism)[cite: 1].

questions.question: In UML Use Case diagrams, a relationship that describes mandatory execution of another use case is represented by:
questions.explanation: The `<<include>>` relationship indicates that a base use case explicitly and unconditionally includes another[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which UML diagram displays object interactions ordered in chronological sequence along a vertical lifeline?
questions.explanation: Sequence diagrams model message exchanges between objects over time along lifelines[cite: 1].

questions.question: In a UML Class diagram, a filled black diamond symbol (◆) denotes:
questions.explanation: A filled diamond represents Composition, where child object lifecycles are strictly tied to the parent[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which design pattern guarantees that a class has only one single instance and provides global access to it?
questions.explanation: The Singleton pattern restricts class instantiation to a single object instance[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which design pattern notifies dependent objects automatically when a subject object undergoes state changes?
questions.explanation: The Observer pattern establishes a one-to-many dependency so dependent objects receive automatic notifications upon subject updates[cite: 1].

questions.question: In a UML class diagram, the symbol '-' before an attribute name specifies which visibility level?
questions.explanation: In UML, `-` indicates private visibility (`+` public, `#` protected, `~` package)[cite: 1].

questions.question: In the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern, which component handles user input and updates the model?
questions.explanation: The Controller component intercepts user input, processes business logic calls, and mutates the Model[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which block in exception handling executes unconditionally regardless of whether an exception occurred?
questions.explanation: The `finally` block always executes to handle resource cleanup regardless of exception execution[cite: 1].

questions.question: Brooks' Law regarding software project management states that:
options: Adding people to a late project speeds up development proportionally
Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later
Software testing eliminates all latent defects
Defect density decreases linearly with team size
questions.explanation: Brooks' Law asserts that adding developers to a delayed project increases communication overhead and delays completion further[cite: 1].
